chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Abu al-Fadl al-Makfuf (the author of Al-Arabiyya), from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl al-Taqi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about a male slave who marries a free woman, what is the status of the child? He said: 'Free.' I said: 'And if a free man marries a slave woman?' He said: 'The child is attached to the free parent. If the mother is free, he is freed with his mother, and if the father is free, he is freed with his father.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of a child born to a slave father and a free mother in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle that a child born to a mixed-status union (one slave, one free) inherits the freedom of the free parent, ensuring emancipation through that lineage. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on social mobility and the removal of hereditary slavery constraints, distinguishing it from other schools that may prioritize the mother's status. The narration underscores the practical implication that the child's legal identity is anchored in the free parent, facilitating their integration into the free community.
